justification: Documentation only, but every claim in it is a measured claim about the live database and the current code, so it carries the same risk profile as code: a wrong number here goes into an employment, contract or licensing conversation and cannot be walked back. Three files under docs/architecture/ — SYSTEM_TECHNICAL.md (three Mermaid diagrams: what gets stored, what gets served, one address end to end), SYSTEM_INTEGRATED.md (the two-pile story view with assurance-ladder colouring and the seven gates), VERIFICATION.md (one row per box, arrow and count, each with the SQL or the file and line that produced it). No application code is touched. The risk this report addresses is not a runtime failure — it is a false claim shipped in a document that a hostile reader will check.

pre_impl.existing_data: Prior-art sweep found four existing architecture documents before writing: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (82 lines, dated 2026-05-02), .claude/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (50 lines, 2026-01-30), .claude/docs/ARCHITECTURE_FLOW_AND_UI.md (1,079 lines) and .claude/docs/ARCHITECTURE-LGA-EXPANSION.md (414 lines). The brief named docs/ARCHITECTURE_FLOW_AND_UI.md, which does not exist at that path — it is under .claude/docs/. The two ARCHITECTURE.md files both open with '47,818 provisions', which is the row count of document_id_backup, a backup table; the live figure is 55,696. They are superseded rather than extended, and SYSTEM_TECHNICAL.md section 5 says so explicitly so a future reader does not treat them as current.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Four assumptions were wrong and were corrected before any file was written. (1) The working tree's local main was 51 commits behind origin/main at the time of the first probe; four of the seven named gates did not exist on that stale tree and .github/workflows/ was absent entirely. All evidence was re-gathered against origin/main at af7982a8. (2) The brief assumed the session might lack live DB access; it did not, so every count is measured on 2026-08-09 rather than cited from the 2026-08-08 strategy review. (3) services/CLAUDE.md describes all five satellite products as 'not started' and they are all shipped — that document is excluded as an evidence source. (4) A plain grep for 'sentinel' across services/ matches six modules, which would have put a false Sentinel-2 edge on the diagram; opening each file showed three of them use the word to mean a sentinel value. Only pre_da_history.py and drawdown_verify.py touch imagery.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: New directory docs/architecture/. Nothing existing was edited or deleted. The four prior architecture documents are left in place and cross-referenced with their staleness stated. .qa_report.json is replaced, which is the per-branch convention.

functions.name: read-only DB evidence collection
functions.file_line: ad-hoc script; all SQL reproduced verbatim in docs/architecture/VERIFICATION.md section 1
functions.output: 37 exact counts, each stored beside the SELECT that produced it
functions.if_none: The connection was opened with set_session(readonly=True) and SET statement_timeout = 30000, so a write could not have executed even if one had been written by mistake. Had the connection failed, the fallback was the counts committed in STRATEGY_REVIEW_2026-08-08.md, labelled with that date; it was not needed.

functions.name: Mermaid render check
functions.input: the four fenced mermaid blocks, extracted from the two markdown files by script rather than by hand
functions.output: four SVGs, zero syntax errors, all page-shaped rather than strip-shaped
functions.if_none: mermaid-cli renders a diagram containing the words 'Syntax error' rather than exiting non-zero, so a grep for that string is run over each SVG as well as checking the exit path. All four return zero matches.

functions.input: the three new markdown files under docs/architecture/, passed explicitly with --docs
functions.output: no path and no version findings against these files
functions.if_none: The seven dependency findings it reports are pre-existing repository issues about requirements files and test imports; they are unrelated to this change and are not fixed here.

Four such items exist; the Trigger.dev hop is the substantive one, because its task definitions live in the sibling repository plotdetect-agents which is not checked out here.

queries.query: SELECT count(*) FROM dcp_setback_controls WHERE is_current = TRUE
queries.purpose: Establish how many numeric DCP controls are actually served, as distinct from how many rows the table holds. The diagram shows both 1,071 and 989 because the difference matters: quoting the table size as the served figure would overstate the defensible surface by 82 rows.
queries.file_line: docs/architecture/VERIFICATION.md section 1, the row labelled '989 live'
queries.where_clause: is_current = TRUE — without it the count returns 1,071, which includes superseded rows and the 28 fabricated-value rows that were deliberately set is_current=FALSE rather than deleted, so that the evidence of the defect survives.

queries.query: SELECT count(*) FROM regulatory_provisions WHERE is_current = TRUE AND v2_is_actionable = TRUE
queries.purpose: Establish the served clause count. The raw table count of 55,696 is the number quoted in two stale architecture documents and in older marketing, and it is roughly 2.8x the number a user can actually be shown.
queries.file_line: docs/architecture/VERIFICATION.md section 1, the row labelled '19,957 served'
queries.where_clause: is_current = TRUE AND v2_is_actionable = TRUE — both are required. is_current alone returns 31,469, which includes clauses that are current but are narrative rather than a control.

queries.query: all 37 evidence queries as a set
queries.purpose: Produce every count on every diagram from the live database rather than from a document, so that each figure carries its own reproduction instructions.
queries.file_line: docs/architecture/VERIFICATION.md section 1, one row per query
queries.where_clause: Read-only session throughout: set_session(readonly=True) plus statement_timeout 30s. Every statement is a SELECT and no transaction is opened that could write. The project rule is that a change to this database is immediately live in production, so a documentation task opens the connection read-only rather than relying on each query being careful.

break_it.scenario: A reader checks a count and it does not reproduce
break_it.what_happens: The diagram is wrong and should be corrected.
break_it.how: Every count carries the SELECT that produced it and the date it ran, so the reader can distinguish 'this was never true' from 'this has moved since 9 August'. VERIFICATION.md opens by saying exactly that.
break_it.repro: Run any query in VERIFICATION.md section 1 against the production database.

break_it.scenario: The diagram is read months later and quoted as current
break_it.what_happens: Stale counts presented as measured — the failure mode the strategy review names as the leading source of false premises in this project.
break_it.how: Both files carry the measurement date and the commit hash in their first two lines. The figures that move fastest are the ingest-run count and the certificate and application totals, which change daily; the spatial and DCP counts move rarely.
break_it.repro: Re-run the section 1 queries and compare.

break_it.scenario: A grep-based claim is wrong because the matched word means something else in code
break_it.what_happens: A false edge is drawn — the same class of error as the 'Threat Radar shares the Sentinel-2 pipeline' line that misled three sessions.
break_it.how: This actually happened during the work. Every module matched by the 'sentinel' search was opened; three used it as a programming term. The near-miss is recorded in VERIFICATION.md section 6 rather than quietly fixed, because the record is the useful part.
break_it.repro: grep -rl "sentinel" services/ returns six files; open bushfire_prescreen.py, cdc_screen.py and solar_yield.py and read the matching lines.

break_it.scenario: Evidence is gathered from a stale checkout
break_it.what_happens: Gates that exist are reported as missing, and the whole picture is wrong by 51 commits.
break_it.how: This also happened. The first probe reported four of the seven gates as absent. Comparing local main against origin/main showed it 51 commits behind, so all evidence was re-gathered against origin/main. Every file claim states the commit it was checked at.

break_it.scenario: The dcp_setback_controls count is taken without is_current = TRUE, so 1,071 is quoted as the number of numeric controls actually served
break_it.what_happens: The defensible surface is overstated by 82 rows, and the overstatement includes the 28 fabricated-value rows that were deliberately marked is_current=FALSE rather than deleted. Quoting those as live would republish the exact defect the fabrication guard was built to stop.
break_it.how: Both numbers appear on the diagram and in VERIFICATION.md section 1 — 1,071 rows held, 989 live — with the WHERE clause shown for the second. A reader cannot pick up one without seeing the other.
break_it.repro: SELECT count(*) FROM dcp_setback_controls; then the same with WHERE is_current = TRUE. Compare 1,071 against 989.

break_it.scenario: The regulatory_provisions count is taken without the v2_is_actionable filter, so 55,696 clauses is quoted as the served corpus
break_it.what_happens: The corpus is overstated by roughly 2.8x. This is not hypothetical: 47,818 — a backup table's row count — appears in two committed architecture documents, and inflated corpus figures have appeared in older marketing.
break_it.how: The diagram box reads '55,696 · 19,957 served' so both halves travel together, and VERIFICATION.md section 6 names the two stale documents and the backup table their number came from.
break_it.repro: SELECT count(*) FROM regulatory_provisions; then add WHERE is_current AND v2_is_actionable. Compare 55,696 against 19,957, and note is_current alone gives 31,469.

break_it.scenario: Producing the diagram damages the user's uncommitted work
break_it.what_happens: At the start of this work, four files had both local uncommitted edits and upstream changes, so a checkout would have conflicted or discarded them.
break_it.how: Nothing in the primary working tree was modified while that was true; work was isolated until main had been brought up to date, at which point the conflict no longer existed. The only files this branch adds are new ones under docs/architecture/, plus the replaced .qa_report.json.
break_it.repro: git status --porcelain — the remaining modified files are unrelated to this change.

post_merge.db_reset: None. No migration, no schema change, no write of any kind.
post_merge.secrets: None added. Evidence collection read DATABASE_URL from the existing repository root .env; no credential appears in any committed file.
post_merge.other_repo: The Trigger.dev task definitions in the sibling repository plotdetect-agents remain unverified and are marked as such on the diagram. If that repository is ever checked out alongside this one, the dashed edge can be resolved and the row in VERIFICATION.md section 4 removed.
post_merge.manual_verify: Open both markdown files on GitHub and confirm the four Mermaid blocks render. They render locally under mermaid-cli 10 with zero syntax errors, which is strong evidence but not identical to GitHub's renderer version.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: Any file path, module or version named in the three documents stops resolving in the code — for example if services/pre_da_history.py is renamed, or scripts/falsifiability.py is removed. It reported a genuine finding on the first run against these files, when an earlier draft cited a deleted module's path as evidence that the file no longer exists; the row now cites the deleting commit c6d64edb instead. It does not and cannot check whether a count still matches the database, which is why every count carries its own query.
